title: Plumb
summary: A browser-based tool for architectural and preservation work that produces measured, verifiable photographs of historic buildings and bridges, with a calibrated grid and ruler and C2PA provenance.

narrative.problem: Architectural and preservation work needs photographs that are evidence, not illustrations: images you can measure from, whose location, creator, date and lineage can be verified. The HABS/HAER/HALS documentation standards already require a scale in the photograph.
narrative.decision: C2PA is the provenance backbone: raw captures are signed at ingest and every derivative names its parents as C2PA ingredients, while authoritative measurement happens in server-side post-processing that can be re-run later on the same immutable bytes.
narrative.tradeoff: As a browser app it cannot reach on-device keystore signing, the only route to C2PA Assurance Level 2, so that is deferred; Android Chrome is the primary platform and iOS Safari gets an honestly labelled reduced feature set.
narrative.limitation: It is not survey-grade: achievable accuracy is roughly USIBD LOA20–LOA10 for marker-calibrated single images, measurements are exact only on the calibrated plane, and it does not replace a total station, laser scan or licensed survey.
narrative.caveat: Needs a phone camera over HTTPS; Android Chrome gets the full feature set. Measurement stays disabled until the grid is calibrated, and results are not a licensed survey.

images.alt: Plumb capture screen with an empty camera view listing three steps, a CAL-0 not-to-scale badge, grid and ruler toggles, and Capture and Calibrate panels on the right.
images.caption: The browser client: start the camera, calibrate against something of known size, add a hold-out check, then measure; nothing leaves the device.

images.alt: Printable Plumb calibration target with four checkerboard corner markers, width and height arrows, a form for measured dimensions and a 100 mm check bar.
images.caption: The printed calibration target puts a scale in the frame, the requirement landmark documentation standards set for measured photographs.

images.alt: Section diagram of a camera photographing a wall with a cornice projecting 600 mm, showing how the cornice reads about 24 mm wrong when only the wall plane is calibrated.
images.caption: The field guide's main warning: Plumb is exact only on the calibrated surface, so projecting features need their depth entered or a second plane.
